Chapter 12: Praying for Wisdom and Decision-Making
Life really is a series of choices, isn’t it? Sometimes, the pressure of making the right decision can feel almost crushing. If you’re a parent, you know how tough it is to watch your grown kids stand at those big crossroads—maybe they’re thinking about a new job, a relationship, or a major financial step. You probably wish you could just hand them the answers. But here’s the thing—wisdom isn’t something we can simply give away. It’s something each person has to uncover for themselves.
Picture this: a daughter calls her parents, wrestling with the idea of a big move. They listen, they share their perspective, but deep down, they realize it’s her decision to make. So what do they do? They pray. They ask for clarity, for a sense of peace, for her to really notice when the right direction becomes clear. In the end, she chooses a path that challenges her and helps her grow in ways none of them could have predicted.
Most of us don’t realize just how much wisdom is shaped by experience. It’s those mistakes we make, those times we learn to pay attention to that quiet voice inside, that really matter. And for parents, it’s so tempting to want to shield their kids from every bit of pain. But sometimes, stepping back and praying is the best thing they can do—asking for discernment, for courage, and for the kind of humility you can’t teach in a conversation.
Imagine a father watching his son navigate a tricky relationship. Instead of jumping in to fix things, he prays: for honesty, for the ability to see things clearly, and for the strength to make tough decisions. Over time, his son finds his footing, picking up lessons that will stay with him for years.
Wisdom isn’t about having all the answers. It’s about asking the right questions, being patient, and trusting that the right path will reveal itself. As parents, you can pray for your kids to keep their hearts open, to seek out wise voices, and to learn from every experience—good or bad.
